newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army captain cleared of rape in sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army captain cleared of rape in sex scandal.

text.p: In a suprise settlement, the military agreed Thursday to clear an Army captain of rape charges but still found him guilty of consensual sex with a female trainee.

Capt. Derrick Robertson, the highest-ranking defendant in the sex scandal at Aberdeen Proving Ground training base, faces a possible maximum sentence of 10-1/2 years in prison, plus dismissal from the service.
Col. Ferdinand Clervi, the presiding judge, accepted the plea agreement and was to sentence Robertson later Thursday.

Robertson, 31, had been accused of raping one of five female soldiers who had come to him to complain of sexual harassment by another officer. If convicted of the charges, he could have faced life imprisonment.

He admitted he had consensual sex with Pvt. Theresa Shannon, 20, in his off-base house on Sept. 14, 1996, pleading guilty to adultery, consensual sodomy, conduct unbecoming an officer and dereliction of duty. He denied charges of rape, forcible sodomy and indecent assault.
Hours before a pre-trial hearing was scheduled to begin, the prosecution accepted the plea arrangement that dropped all charges of sexual assault.

In pleading for leniency, Robertson said he was lonely and in the midst of a divorce when he slept with Shannon. She initiated the relationship when she placed his hand on her breast while they spoke alone in his office, he said.
They began kissing and one week later Shannon accepted his invitation to come to his house at night, he said. He admitted that night of sex was improper but insisted it was consensual.

A stellar soldier, Robertson rose from private to company commander during 11 years in the service. The defence pictured him as an upright person who pulled himself "up from the dirt of East Texas, then became a solider," veering off course only once when he had sex with a woman under his command.
His commanders had described him as "inspirational," "simply outstanding," and "a man who brightens everyone's life," according to recommendations that were read in court.

But prosecutor Capt. Theresa Gallagher said Robertson had abused his trust by treating the recruit as "his sexual play toy," adding: "There is no place in the military for someone whose selfish sexual desires, his lust, comes above the needs of his country and the defence of its sons and daughters."

Gallagher noted that Shannon had come to Robertson to complain that she had been sexually harassed by Drill Sgt. Delmar Simpson, who is facing separate charges. In taking advantage of her trust and vulnerability, the prosecutor said, Robertson abused his office.

The prosecution asked that Robertson serve two years in prison, be dismissed from the service, sacrifice his salary and pay a fine of $5,000 to compensate for some of his training, as well as "costing this Army one female recruit."

Robertson sobbed as he described the humiliation of being labeled a rapist by Army officials on network television. His lawyer, Maj. Jerome Murphy, said Robertson had already been punished by the publicity and should be be given only an administrative discharge.
